A1.justification: Both PDFs describe XLOGOMINIPROG, with matching original datasets, methods, and results. Text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison. V1 ends after its references; v2 includes readable Appendices A-D.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original model evaluations, fine-tuning results, skill analyses, and training curves on 85 real-world and 1,000 synthetic evaluation tasks.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A-C retain the original experiments and add model evaluations, dataset-quality annotations, failure analyses, and transfer experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed synthetic-data generation, supervised LoRA training, cross-entropy objective, and emulator-driven reweighting procedure remain unchanged, including Equation 1. V2 expands their documentation and tests additional models and input representations without introducing a new core algorithmic component.

E1.justification: V2 adds general Python synthesis evaluations on HumanEval and MBPP, including their enhanced '+' test suites, and evaluates perturbed grid and constraint scenarios. The original REAL and SIM-EVAL datasets are retained under the names BASIC and SIMEVAL.

E2.justification: Figure 6 retains the original comparators and adds o1, two DeepSeek-R1 distilled models, GPT-4o, and models from the LLaVA, InternVL2, Qwen2-VL, NVLM-D, and Molmo families. A fine-tuned LLaVA comparator is also added, substantially broadening the evaluated comparison set.

E3.justification: New protocols include three-shot/CoT prompting, NL-versus-ASCII representations, training on approximately 72k samples with math tasks excluded, manual quality scoring, and cross-domain pass@1 evaluation. Reasoning models introduce distinct sampling and token budgets; o1's SIMEVAL score excludes 25 unanswered tasks and uses 975 tasks. Original benchmark splits and primary metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds explanation-based failure attribution, constraint and spatial perturbations of ten selected tasks, dataset-quality assessment, prompting and representation sensitivity, withheld-math transfer, and general-programming retention tests. The original epoch analysis moves to Figure 16a; new SIMEVAL learning curves and a perturbed-code case study supplement it.

E5.justification: Retained fine-tuning results continue to report means and standard errors across five random seeds. V2 repeats this practice for additional comparisons without documenting an increased original run count or introducing new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The original Figure 6 result entries are preserved, but substantial new results appear. These include o1's 76.47% BASIC success rate and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B's 44.71% BASIC and 32.90% SIMEVAL rates. New transfer experiments report fine-tuning deficits of 3.1-5.8 percentage points on general Python benchmarks, alongside numerous failure, quality, and ablation results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces an overall-quality score defined as the minimum of three component ratings: visual appeal, grid-element utility, and code quality. This is a limited new mathematical score definition; the task formalization, DSL, synthesis objective, and resampling equation remain unchanged, with no new proofs or theorems.

C1.justification: The benchmark and synthetic-data/emulator fine-tuning contributions remain central. V2 adds failure diagnosis as an explicit contribution and conclusion, extends the named outperformance claim to DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, and removes v1's concluding statement that the best evaluated base model achieves only 20%.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies vision's benefits because textual inputs already encode the grid, and emphasizes reasoning capabilities. New interpretations address model-specific failures, selection and distribution-shift effects, limited math transfer, and possible forgetting on general coding tasks. Limitations now explicitly identify missing advanced programming concepts, while retaining the binary-feedback limitation.

D1.justification: Appendices A, B, and D supply details that v1 only promised: generation parameters, sampling procedures, model identifiers, LoRA settings, learning rates, batch sizes, hardware, training and resampling times, beta=1, and full prompts. V2 also supplies a benchmark repository link. These additions substantially improve documentation of the existing pipeline.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the dedicated spatial-planning/navigation discussion with multimodal-benchmark positioning, including MM-Vet and Vibe-Eval, and emphasizes educational applicability. References also expand substantially to cover reasoning and vision models, curriculum learning, prompting, SMT solving, inference infrastructure, and enhanced code evaluation.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: generation and fine-tuning details move into appendices, the experimental narrative is rewritten around vision, reasoning, and fine-tuning, and comparative and failure analyses receive separate subsections. Epoch analysis moves to Appendix C.3, limitations become standalone, and dataset terminology is standardized.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, expands and regroups Figure 6, and redraws the skill radars with additional models and linear axes replacing Figure 7's logarithmic presentation. It adds failure, quality, and transfer displays, platform screenshots, and full prompt figures; the original epoch plot becomes part of the two-panel Figure 16.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical validation and supplies reproducibility details that v1 only promised. Failure, perturbation, and transfer tests clarify what fine-tuning achieves and where it fails, while broader model comparisons improve the benchmark's usefulness. Conflicting o1 identifiers in Figures 6 and 13 and its different SIMEVAL denominator limit that comparison, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
